slides.title: Data centers became a ballot issue
body: The Nov 3 midterms gave Democrats full control of Congress, with Republicans in the White House. TechCrunch says anger over **data centers**, the large facilities that house the computers powering AI, is becoming a political force.

slides.title: Voters are wary of AI
body: An NBC exit poll found more than half of respondents think AI will do **more harm than good**. Almost 80% oppose data centers in their neighborhoods, and almost 60% called them a crucial or major factor in their vote.

slides.title: An Ohio county bans data centers
body: In Ohio, the county where Meta had planned a 700,000-square-foot data center passed a ban. OpenAI has eyed a **$500 billion** data center in the state, backed by more than $100 billion in Nvidia financing.

slides.title: The fastest-growing market may shift
body: Texas is the fastest-growing US data center market. Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the governor's race after pushing for a **moratorium**, and Democrats will take the Texas House for the first time in 24 years, MIT Technology Review reports.

slides.title: More limits could follow
body: TechCrunch lists likely next steps: more construction moratoriums, or making data centers pay for their own **grid upgrades**. Goldman Sachs predicts delays in states like Georgia and Texas. A national moratorium bill could face a veto.

slides.title: Following through is hard
body: In Texas, no single office decides whether a project goes ahead, MIT Technology Review notes, and construction unions that backed some Democrats may push back. Even among Democrats, a **blanket freeze** is contested, says Nadine Smith of the racial justice group Color of Change.

facts.text: The November 3 midterm results gave Democrats full control of Congress, with Republicans in the White House. Anger over data centers, the large facilities that house the computers powering AI, is becoming a political force.

An NBC exit poll: more than half of respondents believe AI will do more harm than good; almost 80% are against the building of data centers in their neighborhoods; almost 60% said data centers were a crucial or major factor in their vote.

Ohio: the county where Meta had planned a 700,000-square-foot facility passed a ban on data centers. OpenAI has eyed a $500 billion data center in Ohio, backed by more than $100 billion in financing from Nvidia.

Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US. Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the governor's race against Greg Abbott; Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years. During her campaign Hinojosa began pushing for a full-fledged moratorium.

Likely next steps include more construction moratoriums or requiring data centers to pay for their own power grid upgrades. Goldman Sachs predicts data center construction delays in states like Georgia and Texas. A nationwide-moratorium bill by Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez would also face a possible veto.
No single office in Texas decides whether a project goes ahead. Democrats pushing for a moratorium might face pushback from the construction unions that supported some of their campaigns.
Nadine Smith of Color of Change: "Even among Democrats, a blanket freeze is contested."
